TwinShare

the twin share of the cycle
Proved in Leanring 3Patterns, admissibility and the Hardy-Littlewood constants

Among all survivors of a cycle, the twin survivors make up exactly the product over the wheels from 3 up of the wheel size minus 2 over the wheel size minus 1. That product splits into the partial twin-prime constant times the coprime share.

Claims (2)

twin_share_eq_prod
proved in Lean
The twin survivors of the cycle, as a share of the survivors of the pattern {0}, equal the product over the odd active wheels of the wheel size minus 2 over the wheel size minus 1.
/-- **The twin share of the cycle.** For the wheels below `limit`, the twin
survivors of the cycle divided by the survivors of the pattern `{0}` equal
the product, over the active wheels other than 2, of the wheel size minus 2
over the wheel size minus 1. -/
def twin_share_eq_prod : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : Nat,
    ((wheel_survivors limit).card : Real) / (wheel_survivors_gen {0} limit).card
      = ∏ q ∈ (active_primes limit).erase 2, ((q : Real) - 2) / ((q : Real) - 1)
Rests on: SurvivorCount.twin_survivor_countSurvivorCount.general_survivor_count

twin_share_split
proved in Lean
That product is the partial twin-prime constant times the share the odd wheels leave open.
/-- **The twin share, split.** The same product equals the partial twin-prime
constant (one minus one over the wheel size minus 1, squared, over the odd
active wheels) times the share the odd active wheels leave open (the wheel
size minus 1 over the wheel size). -/
def twin_share_split : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : Nat,
    ∏ q ∈ (active_primes limit).erase 2, ((q : Real) - 2) / ((q : Real) - 1)
      = (∏ q ∈ (active_primes limit).erase 2, (1 - 1 / ((q : Real) - 1) ^ 2))
        * ∏ q ∈ (active_primes limit).erase 2, ((q : Real) - 1) / (q : Real)
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.TwinShare.twin_share_split_holds ↗
